title: Yugoslavia
capsule: Formed on 1 December 1918 as the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes and renamed Yugoslavia in 1929, the interwar kingdom was dominated by Serbian dynastic rule under King Alexander I, who imposed a royal dictatorship in 1929 to suppress ethnic and political conflict. Assassinated in Marseille in 1934, Alexander was succeeded by his young son Peter II under a regency led by Prince Paul, whose 1941 alignment with the Axis triggered a coup and the German-led invasion and dismemberment of the country; the occupied kingdom's government-in-exile lost ground to Josip Broz Tito's communist Partisans, and the monarchy was formally abolished on 29 November 1945.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The interwar Yugoslavia's territory is precisely defined by post-WWI treaties (Trianon, Rapallo, Saint-Germain); the dataset's to date of 1946 reflects the socialist reorganization rather than territorial dissolution.
